```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. B names a specific target customer: a Wisconsin public adjuster plus an affiliated roofing contractor. A must cold-start on the Shopify App Store with zero reviews, zero ranking and no named prospect.",
    "B's price anchors are sourced and higher, at $65–$250/mo (ClaimWizard, claimOS, Claim Titan, AdjustCRM). A single B customer is therefore worth more than several A installs, and B's competitors charge for entry rather than giving it away.",
    "A's own brief shows heavy price compression. Zigpoll, Fairing and Compra all have free tiers, and Simplify starts at $9.99. A new entrant has little room to convert a merchant to paid quickly.",
    "A's brief undercuts its own speed case. Its poster-child success, Zigpoll, took two years to gain traction despite an experienced founder. The brief also says incumbents can outbid newcomers in App Store CPC ads, and that competitor comparison pages already dominate organic search.",
    "B's demand evidence is thin: one ops-lead quote, one Reddit post and industry commentary. It is still comparable to A's, which rests on a single Reddit merchant quote. For a 90-day test, a direct conversation with a known buyer beats inferred marketplace demand.",
    "B's weaknesses matter more for scaling than for the first sale: only 188 in-state licensees, compliance duties under Wisconsin's data-security law, and scope creep toward full claim-lifecycle features. They do not block a first paying contract with one firm."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A infers 'existing willingness to pay for an automated tool' from one Reddit merchant who said customers would not take post-purchase calls. That is a single anecdote with no price signal. Free incumbents already serve this pain, so it does not show the merchant would pay a new, unreviewed app.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's main advantage, an identified customer pair, is asserted but not evidenced. B's brief itself lists 'Is the named customer's commitment real/recurring or informal?' as open. If that commitment is informal or absent, B loses most of its edge, though its higher price point and direct-sale path would still compare favorably to A's saturated, free-tier marketplace. B's six-week build also carries real compliance and scope risk."
}
```
